items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: I think I worked with Cole a few months anyway; I don't know how long we worked together until I left the band.

ctx.x: enthused. He come into a fine band, a nice bunch of guys -- and lucky, win the money, too. So he was happy. I can't say how happy he was, but he was very happy.

And the next day, well, naturally the games keep on, you know; we play every day. And he didn't do so well the next day. The fellows kind of got in his money. Taken all of his little winnings and a little bit out of his pocket. Then it wasn't so nice. But he just stuck with it. He stayed in them days, and he was trying to get lucky again. Which he never did get lucky again. I never seen him win any more money til I had left the band. I don't know if he ever won any more. I stayed there... Let me see. I think I…
But he was a beautiful saxophone player, believe me. Good clarinettist.
